About the Architect
Jef Aerts is a systems architect and operational operator focused on structured knowledge governance, multi-provider AI gateway security, and deterministic data/accounting systems. This book presents three standalone architecture builds (SSoT, Balaerion, and Syndicate) plus the Signal design suite, emphasizing failure modes, design trade-offs, and automated verification over raw code dumps.

Pillar I: SSoT Highlights ([Status: Designed + Prototype])
The Constraint
Designed under strict enterprise compliance blockers that prohibited standard off-the-shelf Knowledge Management Systems (such as Confluence, Zendesk KMS, or Salesforce Knowledge).
The Architecture
Specified as a zero-license-cost knowledge operations system ([Status: Designed], interactive flows [Status: Prototype]) built on standard enterprise workspace primitives (Enterprise Wiki, Relational Governance Base, and ChatOps Bot). The reference model spans 40 markets and 3,055 public reference nodes (3,000+ nodes, Chapter 2: System Architecture) using a normalized 11-table schema (Chapter 4: Relational Database Schema) and 14 conversational bot commands (Chapter 6: Bot Command Reference).
Verification & Business Case (Standardized Lean Reference Model)
Modeled using Lean Six Sigma DMADV methodology on a standardized 100-seat enterprise reference scenario, yielding a modeled gross recoverable value range of EUR 198,000 to EUR 297,000 / year (40% to 60% friction recovery; EUR 188,100 to EUR 287,100 / year net after illustrative EUR 9,900 / year maintenance; Chapter 1). Governance specifies 10 automated controls (5 scheduled scanners, 5 event detectors) plus an external dead-man heartbeat (HB-001, Chapter 5), 5 Internal Container Access Tiers (I-0 to I-4) across 6 Operating Roles (Chapter 7), and a 98.2% (~98%) reduction in metered platform automation runs.

Pillar II: Balaerion Highlights ([Status: Prototype + Designed])
The Constraint
Teams adopting free-tier or multi-vendor LLM endpoints routinely expose unmasked client identifiers across non-EU providers, hardcode rotating model IDs, or allow generative prose to invent company registration facts.
The Architecture
Architected as a dual-mode serverless AI gateway (Mode A 12-provider standalone workbench + Mode B ProspectHub 7-state GTM workspace; Balaerion I) routing 23 AI personas (7 Mode A utilities + 16 Mode B specialists; Balaerion IV) across strict lane: eu and lane: general boundaries (Balaerion III). ProspectHub enriches accounts via a Hybrid 8-Collector Card-Free OSINT Layer (3 zero-key built-in collectors for DNS/SPF/DMARC, HTML CMS/Pixel/CMP head scan, and FR SIREN Open API + 5 optional free-tier collectors; Balaerion V) and compiles grounded briefs directly into Signal Studio (16:9) and Signal Press (A4) (Balaerion VI).
Verification & Safeguards
Pre-dispatch regex and lane guards block VAT, IBAN, email, and eu -> general cross-lane leaks (HTTP 403) before any socket opens; throttled eu endpoints fail closed to deterministic Replay rather than crossing lanes; and public calibration fixtures use synthetic Belgian KBO 0123.456.789 (which intentionally fails mod-97 check 49 != 89 so it can never match a real company). Explore the recorded sandbox in the Balaerion Interactive Demo.

Pillar III: Syndicate Highlights ([Status: Prototype (Simulation) + Designed])
The Constraint
Group sports prediction pools and recreational tipgames suffer from two structural defects: intuition-driven picks ignore expected-goals (xG) variance, low-score draw clustering, and bookmaker overround skew, while shared spreadsheets silently dilute existing participants whenever members enter or exit mid-season.
The Architecture
Designed as a strictly non-financial statistical simulation and unit-accounting system (Syndicate I): a Dixon-Coles (1997) correlated Poisson scoreline engine paired with Shin (1993) insider overround de-vigging (Syndicate II), a quorum-gated selection card state machine with a hard T - 15m pre-kickoff lock (Syndicate III), a fixed-scale NUMERIC(18,6) unit-share Net Asset Value (NAV) ledger denominated in non-monetary virtual units (VU) (Syndicate IV), and proper scoring calibration (Brier, Log-Loss, CLV) plus 1,000-path Monte Carlo Quarter-Kelly drawdown stress testing (Syndicate V).
Verification & Safeguards
Enforces inter-matchday dealing cutoffs (blocking stale-NAV entry while selection cards are in play), ROUND_HALF_EVEN rounding with residual sweep, UNIQUE (idempotency_key) settlement protection, and PostgreSQL REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE triggers. Exercise the 36-club synthetic league table, Dixon-Coles + Shin lab, 1,000-run Monte Carlo simulator, and VU ledger in the Syndicate Simulation Demo.

Live Full-Stack Workspace (Hiring Manager & Reviewer Access)
This portfolio operates across two deliberately separated surfaces so every reviewer can inspect both clean-room specifications and live full-stack execution without risking free-tier quota abuse:

II. System Architecture, Schema and Build Specification
Focus: Topology, Schema, Bot Operations, Console & Disaster Recovery · Status: Designed (Interactive flows: Prototype)

1. Purpose and Scope
This is the target architecture specification ([Status: Designed]) for the Autonomous Knowledge Architecture: a standardized enterprise advertising knowledge library modeling 3,055 public reference files (3,000+ nodes across 40 reference markets) plus a governed internal operations layer (~1,200 initial legacy documents), deployed in a private workspace wiki space, governed by a normalized 11-table relational database, and operated via an authenticated conversational application (Bot).
Two different starting states. The public layer is greenfield: nothing exists initially, and files are drafted with AI assistance after primary-source claim verification by human reviewers. The internal layer models a legacy estate: documents spread across multiple owners with inconsistent ACLs, requiring scripted discovery, consolidation, and container-level permission repair.

2. Platform Prerequisites ([Status: Designed])
Established as pre-implementation readiness gates.

3. Content Architecture & Topology
3.1 Space Topology
One private team space, two root nodes.

Visibility: Private. Nodes are invisible to workspace members until container access is explicitly granted, establishing a deny-by-default access boundary.
Root node 1: Public_Information_Layer (Greenfield reference model: 3,055 nodes across 40 markets + GLB).
Root node 2: Internal_Operations_Layer (Legacy migration model: ~1,200 initial nodes, scaling to ~2,000 by Year 3).

A second space would double the administration surface and break cross-linking between an internal SOP and the public file it governs. Hence, two root nodes within one space.
3.2 Folder Tree & File Limits

7. Document Lifecycle & State Machine
7.1 Asynchronous Publish Sequence
Publishing is a physical node move, not a permission change. It is executed asynchronously to prevent API timeout race conditions.

Reviewer approves via interactive webhook card.
Server ACKs the callback within 3 seconds to satisfy platform timeout limits.
Bot queries the API for the target node token.
Bot executes the document move operation.
Critical Verification: Bot polls the async task ID. Once complete, it queries the node again to assert parent_node_token matches the intended market folder.
Commit: ONLY upon verification does the Bot write Publication State = Published to T1.
Document dynamically inherits the market branch permissions.
Bot writes PUBLISH transaction to T10.


8. Bot & API Layer Operations
8.1 API Throttling & Fault Tolerance

Batch Writes: T1 and T2 updates are chunked at 500 records per batch call with whole-chunk rollback handling.
429 Backoff: The system detects HTTP 429 (Rate Limit Exceeded) responses, reads the suggested wait-time header, and implements an exponential backoff sequence (Max 5 retries before logging F-011 Fault).

8.2 Core Conversational Commands
Agents operate the library via DM or channel commands (14 total commands documented in Chapter VI: 7 core utilities + 7 domain extensions).



Command
Action / Resolution




@Bot ask [query]
Quick-answer endpoint. Facet-extracts the query, searches T1, returns the single best file link plus a 2-line text extract.


@Bot check [vertical] [market]
Fast compliance screen. Returns policy tier and gating requirements.


@Bot gap [question]
Autonomously writes a T3 Gap Tracker record and notifies the market lead for content creation.


@Bot reconcile [CC]
Admin-only. Triggers manual on-demand state and permission reconciliation.




9. Operational Integrity (Self-Healing Sub-Routines)
9.1 Database vs. Wiki State Reconciliation (SC-003)
Because wiki node moves are asynchronous and emit no webhooks, the Database and the Wiki can diverge silently. 

Forward Check: Queries all T1 rows marked Published, fetches the actual wiki node via API, and asserts the parent node matches the expected folder. Detects F-027 (Published in Database, stuck in Staging).
Reverse Check: Enumerates children of every live market folder. Asserts each has a corresponding Published T1 row. Detects F-028 (Live in Wiki, missing from Database).

9.2 The Mover Protocol (DT-002)
When a user changes market scopes in T4, the system must sever old access to prevent privilege accumulation.

Revoke First: Script enumerates departing market branch tokens and executes permission-member delete.
Grant Second: Standard provisioning script runs for the new market scope.
Reassign Ownership: Bot queries T1 for records owned by the mover in the old scope and triggers an interactive card to the FLM to reassign file ownership. 


10. Console (Custom Application Interface)
Console ([Status: Designed], interactive specification [Status: Prototype]) is the administrative operating surface for the platform, designed as a custom frontend application loading directly inside the database interface via a native JS SDK.
Architectural Decision: Why a native JS SDK instead of a Standalone Web App?
A standalone web app writing via a service token attributes every system change to "The Bot". A native JS SDK loads client-side and runs under the signed-in user's identity. This preserves human attribution in the record history, a strict requirement for enterprise auditability.
Console Capabilities:

Batch Import & Dry Run: Chunked 500-record bulk imports with full rollback handling. Validates every row locally before attempting API writes.
Permission Inspection: Reverse lookup mapping showing effective access limits for any user, resolving the delta between Role, Branch Grant, and Publication State.
Publish Queue Management: Surfacing orphaned nodes (F-028) and stuck publishes (F-027) with 1-click re-issue capabilities.


11. Measurement & Declarative KPIs
Database tables hold current state, not history. The platform requires a snapshot engine to track trends. 
The Version Trap Mitigation:
If a KPI definition (e.g., "Files overdue") changes its filter criteria, historical trend lines silently corrupt because they compare two different measurements. 

Solution: KPIs are defined declaratively as JSON data in T-KPI-03. Any change to a KPI's filter logic automatically increments the Definition Version. Trend charts spanning a version change show a physical break marker on the UI, preventing confident but factually wrong reporting.


12. Disaster Recovery & Rollback ([Status: Designed])
The architecture specifies external extraction to satisfy enterprise RTO/RPO targets, rather than relying on time-bounded native platform trash or restore windows.



Element
Specification

Nightly. All operational tables export to CSV/XLSX via the scheduled export API.


Document Export
Weekly. Full document content exported to DOCX/PDF.


Structural Map
Weekly. Full branch map (Node tokens, paths, permission grants) exported to JSON.


Destination
EU-region external object store (preserves residency outside the workspace vendor environment).


RPO / RTO
RPO: 24 hours. RTO: 8 hours for Database, 48 hours for document corpus.


Pre-Destructive Rule
Any bulk deletion or state rollback requires a fresh, verified export before the script executes.




13. Target Deployment Rollout Sequence ([Status: Designed])
Specified as a 9-stage gated rollout sequence (Stage 0 through Stage 8) to isolate failure modes before multi-market scale-out:

Stage 0 (Sandbox Stress Test): Stress-test child-node and tree-depth limits using synthetic fixtures.
Stage 1 (Container Skeleton): Provision the dual-root private space, staging branches, and archive container.
Stage 2 (Relational Schema): Deploy all 11 tables across the Data Layer (9 tables) and Audit Layer (2 tables) in strict foreign-key order.
Stage 3 (Access Matrix Seeding): Seed T4 with the standardized 100-seat reference team (6 operating roles) and verify Agent Lockdown (AGT View-Only).
Stage 4 (Bot & Webhook Harness): Deploy conversational handlers, 3-second callback ACK queues, and HTTP 429 exponential backoff harnesses.
Stage 5 (Automated Control Loop): Enable the 5 scheduled scanners, 5 event detectors, and external dead-man heartbeat monitor in shadow mode.
Stage 6 (Single-Market Validation Gate): Publish all 75 standard market templates for one reference pilot market (e.g., NL) and hold exit criteria across a 14-day burn-in target.
Stage 7 (Multi-Market Wave Scale-Out): Expand across the remaining 39 reference markets while running parallel Document Storage API discovery (D1 to D4) on legacy internal folders.
Stage 8 (Internal Estate Migration): Strip legacy per-document ACLs and relocate internal files into the 15 container-governed areas (I-0 to I-4).

III. Design Methodology (DMADV)
Focus: Lean Six Sigma DMADV (Greenfield) & DMAIC (Legacy Estate)

1. Methodology Selection: Why DMADV?
The public-information layer of the architecture had no incumbent. There was no existing process producing the required market documentation, no defect rate to measure, and no baseline to improve against. 
Applying the standard DMAIC (Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control) methodology here would have required inventing a baseline, and an invented baseline produces an invented improvement. 
Because we were designing a system that did not previously exist, the project utilized DMADV (Define, Measure, Analyze, Design, Verify), the core methodology of Design for Six Sigma (DFSS).

2. Voice of the Customer (VOC) & CTQ Translation
A system designed to optimize for management will fail the end-user. The primary customer is the operational agent; a library that satisfies QA but goes unused by agents is a silent failure.

3. Risk Mitigation (FMEA)

F1 dominates the risk profile. Severity is 10 because false advice is the worst possible outcome. Detection is 8 because a plausible AI hallucination reads exactly like a correct fact. The mitigation strategy attacked the Detection score.

4. The Verification Protocol (Attacking F1)
To mitigate the RPN 560 risk of AI hallucination, the architecture strictly separated generation from verification.
The Rule: Never write a perishable claim from memory or AI output.
A perishable claim is anything that could change or varies by source (e.g., UI paths, API limits, policy thresholds, compliance rules). Confidence from an AI model during generation is not evidence of current accuracy.

Identify every perishable claim before writing a draft. Writing first anchors the author to the generated text, even against a contradicting result.
Search each claim individually against primary sources.
If primary sources conflict, document the conflict. Do not silently pick the one that sounds more confident.
If a claim cannot be verified, explicitly flag it as unverifiable. An honest "could not confirm as of [date]" is worth more than a confident, wrong answer.


5. Verification Phase: Single-Market Validation Gate ([Status: Designed])
Rather than a soft launch, the architecture defines a controlled single-market validation experiment (Stage 6, e.g., NL reference wave: 75 market templates across all domains) that must pass four target CTQ gates before multi-market scale-out (39 remaining reference markets in Stage 7):
Target Verification Gates against CTQs:

V1 (CTQ-1): External 30-query benchmark target: >=90% resolution within  clicks or 1 command.
V2 (CTQ-3): Measurement System Analysis (MSA) target on Market Specificity: three calibrated reviewers must reach >80% inter-rater agreement on the "swap-the-country-name" test before live approval authority is granted.
V3 (Effort Model): Pilot timesheet tracking validates the modeled baseline assumption (0.25 person-days per verified file) before wave budgeting locks.
V6 (CTQ-7 & 8): Scheduled scanners and permission reconciliation jobs must run across a 14-consecutive-night burn-in gate with zero unexplained faults and zero permission divergence before multi-market expansion is authorized.


6. Parallel Track: DMAIC for the Legacy Internal Estate ([Status: Designed])
While the greenfield public layer uses DMADV, the ~1,200 legacy internal documents model an existing estate with measurable defects (broken ACLs, orphaned hubs, duplicate SOPs) governed via DMAIC:

Define: Scope the ~1,200 legacy documents across 15 operational areas and 5 discrete internal container access tiers (I-0 to I-4).
Measure: Execute scripted discovery (D1 to D4) via the Document Storage API to baseline broken per-document ACLs, inbound/outbound link hubs, and title duplication clusters.
Analyze: Isolate high-risk link hubs (where moving a document silently breaks downstream navigation) and classify record-class areas (Meeting Notes, Escalations) for retention rather than review cycles.
Improve: Strip all per-document ACLs during migration and relocate documents into container-governed folders so permissions inherit cleanly.
Control: Lock the migrated estate into the nightly permission reconciliation scanner (SC-004) and enforce retention-based archiving.

5.1 T-KPI-03 (KPI Definitions)
Adding a new KPI is a database row, not a code release. 

The Version Trap: If a KPI's numerator filter logic is edited, historical trend lines silently corrupt because they compare two different measurements. To mitigate this, T-KPI-03 auto-increments a Definition Version field whenever logic changes. Snapshots record this version, allowing frontend charts to render a physical break marker on the trend line when underlying logic shifts.
Guarding the Scan Cost: The system estimates the API scan cost before saving a KPI. If a KPI will scan more than 2,000 rows, it automatically locks the Pre-aggregate flag, forcing it to run on a scheduled snapshot rather than rendering live and crippling dashboard load times.

6.1 T10: Bot Interaction Log (Append-Only Within Retention Window)
T10 contains 16 fields and is append-only within its 12-month active retention window: application roles hold zero UPDATE or DELETE privileges on individual rows, and at the 12-month boundary a scheduled administrative job exports a signed archive to EU object storage before purging expired partitions. 6.2 Degraded (F-013a) vs. Halted (F-013b) Audit States
To reconcile high availability with strict auditability (DT-001):

Degraded Mode (F-013a, P2 Warning): When T10 experiences transient API retry latency (>90s acknowledgment delay), the Bot buffers signed audit rows in durable worker queue memory (up to 15 minutes / 500 events) while read queries and read-only scanners continue uninterrupted.
Halted Mode (F-013b, P1 Outage): If T10 persistently rejects writes (credential revocation, schema lock, or buffer exhaustion), all state-mutating Bot commands and Console batch writes halt fail-closed until T10 write confirmation is restored.


7. Operational Constraints & Batch Limits

500 Records Per API Call: Reads and writes are strictly chunked. Wide scans are pre-aggregated via the snapshot engine.
All-or-Nothing Batch Writes: A single bad row fails the 500-record payload. Validation executes locally before chunking.
Agent Lockdown (AGT Role): Agents (60 seats in the 100-seat reference model) are strictly View-Only on all base tables and execute state updates exclusively via conversational Bot commands (@Bot review, @Bot gap).

V. Self-Healing Loop and Fault Taxonomy
Focus: Single Daily Scan, 10 Automated Controls (5 Scanners + 5 Detectors) & 29-Fault Taxonomy · Status: Designed (Simulated in Prototype)

1. Architectural Philosophy of the Loop
A system without an automated governance loop will inevitably decay. Manual auditing fails because it scales linearly with content volume while rot compounds exponentially. 
To maintain bounded state consistency across 3,055 public reference nodes and ~1,200 internal nodes without manual micromanagement, the architecture specifies a continuous 5-phase control loop ([Status: Designed]):
DETECT   --> Scanners and detectors write a fault to the audit log
CLASSIFY --> Assign category, severity (P1 to P4), and correction tier
CORRECT  --> Tier 1 (Automatic) through Tier 4 (Executive Escalation)
VERIFY   --> Re-scan at T+24h. Only then is the fault marked "Resolved"
LEARN    --> Recurring faults trigger systemic configuration changes, not just record patches
Critical Principle: Verification is separate from correction. A correction applied and logged as done is untested. The automated re-scan at T+24 hours is what confirms whether the fix held.

2. Optimized Execution: The Single Daily Scan
Naive workspace implementations attach native per-record date automations inside the database UI, firing roughly 1,700 platform automation runs per month across active review schedules.
Platform Automation Runs vs. External Server Job Runs

Platform Automation Runs: Metered native UI workflow triggers inside the workspace database product (subject to monthly enterprise automation quotas).
External Server Job Runs: Unmetered cron executions on the Bot/worker service calling batched REST APIs.

Rather than firing 1,700 per-record UI triggers, the architecture replaces review-date UI automations with one native daily review-trigger handoff at 07:30 UTC (SC-002):

Efficiency (98.2% Metered Run Reduction): SC-002 consumes 30 platform automation runs per 30-day month against the 1,700 / month per-record baseline (1 - 30 / 1,700 = 98.2%, cited as ~98%), while SC-001, SC-003, SC-004, and SC-005 execute on the external worker cron (120 server cron runs/month, 0 metered UI runs). (For comparison, scheduling 3 daily UI triggers would consume 90 runs = 94.7% reduction, and running all 5 scanners as UI triggers would consume 150 runs = 91.2% reduction.)
Native Date Dependency: Because database automations cannot reliably trigger off formula-derived dates, the Bot copies calculated review dates into a native date field (Review Due (native)) on every write. This is the only date the daily scan reads.

The Escalation Ladder
When a file reaches its review threshold, the daily scan triggers an automated escalation sequence:

Days 1 to 13: Automated direct message card sent to the content owner ("Verify or Update").
Days 14 to 29: Escalation card sent to the Owner, the Space Owner, and the Market First Line Manager (FLM).
Day 30: Automatic Deprecation. If unaddressed, the node is automatically moved to the archive branch, and its state changes to Archived. Leaving unverified policy or operational files in active circulation is a compliance liability worse than an empty folder.

Exemption: High-velocity, record-class internal areas (Meeting Notes, Escalations, Internal Updates) carry a Review Exempt flag. Feeding 720 dated records a year into a review scan creates noise; they are governed via strict retention periods instead.

3. Scanners & Event Detectors ([Status: Designed])

3.1 Watching the Watchman: External Dead-Man's Switch (HB-001, [Status: Designed])
SC-005 (Expected Run Audit Scanner) catches silent failures in SC-001 through SC-004 by checking T10 for missing completion rows. However, if the worker host, cron daemon, or OAuth service token fails completely, SC-005 itself never executes and no internal alarm fires.
To close that single point of failure without adding paid SaaS dependencies, HB-001 specifies an inverted (absence-triggered) heartbeat:

Upon verifying SC-001..SC-004 at 08:00 UTC, SC-005 issues a signed HTTPS GET ping (containing run_date and row count, zero PII) to an independent external heartbeat endpoint.
If no valid ping arrives before 08:15 UTC (15-minute grace window), the external monitor raises an out-of-band P1 Infrastructure Alert directly to both named System Administrators (ADM).
HB-001 is registered separately in facts/facts.json (1 external monitor supervising the 10 internal automated controls).

Missing job runs, 429 exhaustion, audit write latency/failure (F-011..F-015).


E. Access & Security
Permission and scoping breaches
Unauthorized commands, container ACL drift, incomplete offboarding, Mover leakage (F-019..F-023, F-029).



Severity SLA Enforcement: P1 Faults (such as persistent T10 write failure F-013b, restricted ACL exposure F-019, or incomplete leaver deprovisioning F-023) carry a strict 2-hour resolution SLA and escalate to Tier 4.

5. Systemic Learning & Target Operational Readiness Gate
Correction without learning is manual maintenance with extra steps. 
The 3-Strike Rule ([Status: Designed])
If the exact same fault ID occurs 3 or more times within 30 days, the loop halts minor patching and triggers a mandatory Configuration Review. For example, repeated metadata failures in a specific market indicate a provisioning failure in that market's onboarding workflow rather than isolated author mistakes.
Target Operational Exit Criteria ([Status: Designed])
Under the target deployment readiness contract, the self-healing loop is declared operational only after holding all five criteria across a 14-consecutive-day burn-in window:

Zero missed scheduled scanner runs (SC-001 through SC-005 + HB-001 green).
Every fault marked Resolved passing its T+24h verification re-scan.
Zero P1 faults open past their 2-hour SLA.
Zero unresolved state divergence on SC-003 reconciliation runs.
End-to-end pass of one injected synthetic fault across each of Categories A through E.

VI. Conversational Interface & API Specification
Focus: 14 Conversational Commands (7 Core + 7 Domain Extensions), Scoped OAuth & Webhook Card Safeguards · Status: Designed (Command simulator: Prototype)

1. Architectural Philosophy of the Bot
The conversational application (Bot) serves as the primary operational surface for agents during live engagements. To preserve enterprise access boundaries and register integrity, the Bot is not a passive search wrapper; it is an authenticated, auditable execution proxy.
Core Execution Flow:
bot.message.received event
  --> Authenticate sender against the User Access Register (T4)
  --> Parse command, parameters, and enforce strict Market Scoping
  --> Execute operation (Query, State Change, or Gap Generation)
  --> Format interactive webhook response card
  --> Deliver payload and write an audit transaction to T10
Operating Parameters: 

Response SLA: Under 10 seconds end-to-end.
Authentication: Senders must hold an Active status in T4. Deprovisioned senders are blocked and logged.
Auditability: Every invocation writes to the audit log (T10), including rejected commands and out-of-scope queries.


2. Generalized API Permissions & Scope Profile ([Status: Designed])
To execute background jobs and proxy writes without over-privileging user accounts, the Bot authenticates with a short-lived application-scoped OAuth service token (~2-hour TTL, rotated automatically by the worker SDK) restricted to minimal capability scopes:

Implementation Note: Holding OAuth scopes alone is insufficient; the Bot service principal must also be granted explicit collaborator access on both the Data Layer and Audit Layer database applications, and requires read-write knowledge-base node permissions so it can execute physical node moves during publication.

3. The 14 Conversational Commands (7 Core + 7 Domain Extensions)
Agents operate the knowledge architecture via natural-language commands (@Bot [command] [parameter]). The specification defines 14 commands split evenly between core workspace utilities and domain-specific SSoT extensions:
3.1 Core Operational Utilities (7 Commands)

find [topic]: Returns top 3 matching pages, appending staleness warnings when overdue.
my pages: Lists files owned by the sender with live health and review status badges.
health [title]: Computes and returns the 0-100 stepped health score and deduction breakdown.
gap [question]: Writes a structured demand record to the Gap Tracker (T3) and notifies the market lead.
review [title]: Load-bearing for Agent Lockdown. Sole mechanism for View-Only agents (AGT) to log a self-review and advance Last Reviewed Date.
admin faults: Returns open fault queue summary (F-001 to F-029) for ADM callers.
admin users: Exports active scope and role diagnostics from T4 for ADM callers.

3.2 Domain-Specific SSoT Extensions (7 Commands)
Standard workspace bots lack awareness of ISO market codes, regulated verticals, or container reconciliation. Seven domain extensions close that gap:

4. Key Behavioral Safeguards
4.1 The Staleness Warning
For every file returned by a search or query, the Bot checks Days Overdue. If a file is past its review date, the Bot injects a mandatory warning:

This file is 23 days past review. Verify facts before relying on it.

An agent handed a stale file without warning is worse off than one receiving no file at all, as they will act upon obsolete operational rules with misplaced confidence.
4.2 Strict Market Scoping (Default-Deny)
Market scoping is enforced in code on every command before any node content is read. Missing, empty, or malformed scopes fail closed (false), and both user scopes and target market codes are trimmed and normalized to uppercase:
function inScope(user, marketCode) {
  if (!user || typeof user.scope !== 'string' || typeof marketCode !== 'string') {
    return false;
  }
  const target = marketCode.trim().toUpperCase();
  if (!target) return false;
  const tokens = user.scope
    .split(',')
    .map((s) => s.trim().toUpperCase())
    .filter(Boolean);
  if (tokens.length === 0) return false;
  return tokens.includes('ALL') || tokens.includes(target);
}

If an NL-scoped agent queries a MENA market file, the Bot intercepts the request, returns a scope-rejection message, and logs F-021 via DT-004. The Bot never returns content the caller could not reach by navigating the workspace directly.

5. Interactive Webhook Card Safeguards
5.1 The 3-Second Callback ACK Rule
Enterprise chat platforms require an HTTP 200 acknowledgement within 3 seconds of an interactive card button click; exceeding that window triggers automatic webhook retries and duplicate state writes. Acknowledge immediately and enqueue downstream work asynchronously:
app.post('/card', express.json(), async (req, res) => {
  res.status(200).json({ toast: { type: 'info', content: 'Processing...' } });
  setImmediate(() => processCardActionAsync(req.body));
});

5.2 Card Validity Windows (14 Days)
Interactive approval cards carry a 14-day interaction and update validity window. Because approval cards sent to reviewers on leave expire silently, Console's publishing queue (DT-005) flags any pending approval older than 14 days and issues a fresh card rather than leaving drafts stranded in _STAGING/.

VII. Role-Based Access Matrix & Security Architecture
Focus: 4-Layer Permission Topology, 6 Operating Roles vs. 5 Internal Tiers (I-0..I-4), Agent Lockdown & Mover/Leaver IAM · Status: Designed

1. The Four-Layer Access Topology
The architecture relies on a multi-layered security model. Omitting any layer from the governance strategy results in invisible permission drift.



Layer
Control Scope

3. Database

4. Application

1.1 The Two-Mechanism Rule
Layers 2 (Wiki) and 3 (Database) are strictly independent, and both must be explicitly set. This is the single most misunderstood dynamic in enterprise wiki systems.

An agent seeing a database catalog entry for a document they cannot open is correct behavior. The register is an index of what exists, not a bypass around branch grants. If a document title itself is considered sensitive, the document belongs in a restricted internal tier, not the public market tree.

2. Layer 1: The 6 Operating Roles (AGT to ADM)
The architecture models a standardized 100-seat reference team (60 AGT seats + 40 QA, management, and admin seats) across 6 Operating Roles (distinct from the 5 Internal Container Access Tiers defined in Section 5):

Continuity Rule: Two administrators is a hard continuity requirement, not a nicety. The Application Secret and the Archive Branch are restricted strictly to Administrators. A single administrator creates a single point of failure for systemic continuity and offboarding procedures.

3. Layer 2: Wiki Branch Grants
Access is granted at the branch container level, not on individual documents. 
3.1 Inheritance (Applied Once)
A document moved into a branch inherits that branch's permissions at the exact moment of the move. It is not continuously synced.

Consequence: A branch permission grant changed after publication does not automatically reach documents already residing there. Drift is therefore expected, not exceptional.

3.2 Nightly Permission Reconciliation (SC-004)
To counter post-move drift, external cron scanner SC-004 runs nightly against the API:

Reads the Access Matrix (T4) and computes intended grants from the branch map.
Reads actual grants on the wiki branches.
Computes the diff.
On divergence, re-asserts the intended container grant, writes to the Audit Log (T10), and logs fault F-019 or F-020.


4. The Agent Lockdown (Systemic Integrity)
4.1 Specification
Agents (AGT) hold strictly View Only rights on the central database (T1), with no record conditions permitting direct cell edits. Agents cannot write to the register directly.
This is not a downgrade of the Agent role; it is the foundation of the platform's integrity. A register whose accuracy depends on 60 frontline agent seats never typing into the wrong database cell is not governed; it is merely trusted.
4.2 Conversational Proxy
Because agents are locked out of the database interface, they execute all state changes via the Bot. 

@Bot review records a self-review.
@Bot gap writes to the Gap Tracker.
Approval cards manage publication state changes.

Testing Gate: The lockdown relies entirely on the Bot's ability to act as a proxy. If a test agent cannot edit a database cell directly, but successfully updates their review timestamp via @Bot review, the lockdown is successfully operational.

5. The 5 Internal Container Access Tiers (I-0 to I-4)
The internal operations estate spans 15 functional areas governed by 5 Internal Container Access Tiers (I-0 through I-4). Every area carries an explicit Read Tier and Write Tier (never a single combined tier, which would lock frontline agents out of reading SOPs they are forbidden from editing):

6. Identity Lifecycle (Joiner, Mover, Leaver)
Standard systems document onboarding and offboarding. Enterprise systems document Movers, the most frequent and high-risk vector for permission drift.
6.1 The Mover Protocol (DT-002)
When an agent moves between markets but retains ownership of files in their previous market, they retain the ability to edit content outside their new scope, while the incoming agent is locked out.
The Mover Sequence:

Scope change recorded in Access Matrix (T4). Detector DT-002 fires.
Revoke First: The Bot strips all branch tokens for the departing market on the same day. 
Grant Second: Standard provisioning is run for the new market. (Granting first creates a window where the user holds both scopes).
Reassign Ownership: The Bot inventories records owned by the mover in the old scope and assigns them to the new owner (or the First Line Manager if vacant).

6.2 The Leaver Protocol (DT-003)
Order of operations is critical because native workspace trash/recovery windows are time-bounded and deprovisioned account assets do not re-link automatically:

Identify all owned records and reassign to new owners before the final day.
Route the user's Area 15 work-continuity folder through HR/DPO review and transfer approved work records to their manager within 48 hours.
Only after data transfer is confirmed should the account state be changed to Deprovisioned.


7. Application Security & The App Secret
The Application Secret is the most sensitive credential in the system. Compromise allows an actor to impersonate the Bot and read/write every database table, including bypassing the audit log.

Storage: Stored exclusively in the Developer Console and as a single server environment variable. Never in the wiki, database, or a document.
Rotation: Rotated annually. Following rotation, all 14 Bot commands must be tested against a staging environment to confirm the new credential propagates cleanly.
Audit Failure as a P1 Incident: The audit trail (T10) is a primary deliverable. If T10 enters persistent write failure (F-013b), state-mutating operations halt and the event is treated as a P1 Outage.

VIII. Security & Compliance (GDPR Governance Draft)
Focus: Proposed GDPR Lawful-Basis Mapping, Residency vs. Sovereignty & Art. 33 Breach Protocol · Status: Designed (Draft for Legal/DPO Review)

Draft Notice (For Owner & Legal Review - Not Legal Advice): This chapter is an engineering data-protection design draft prepared to structure controller/DPO review under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR). Lawful-basis selections, Legitimate Interests Assessments (LIAs), retention schedules, and erasure exceptions depend on jurisdiction-specific employment law and controller counsel sign-off; nothing below constitutes legal advice or a final legal conclusion.


1. Compliance Position & Governance Context
The reference architecture models personal data across two operational vectors with distinct risk profiles:

Workspace Governance Data: Identity, role-scoping, ramp-milestone, and audit telemetry for the 100-seat internal team.
Internal Layer Data (Area 11): Business-to-business client contact context scoped by market.




Element
Proposed Design Specification

Deploying Organization (subject to local corporate entity mapping).


Data Contact / DPO
Named Data Protection Contact (or statutory DPO where appointed).


Data Processor
Enterprise Workspace Vendor, operating under an executed Art. 28 Data Processing Agreement (DPA).


Reference Framework
EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679).


Proposed Primary Bases
Art. 6(1)(b) Contractual Necessity (where strictly required for role execution) & Art. 6(1)(f) Legitimate Interests (backed by documented LIAs).




2. Data Residency vs. Sovereignty
2.1 The Distinction
Residency and Sovereignty must be evaluated separately. Conflating physical storage location with jurisdictional immunity fails informed procurement and DPO review.

Data Residency (Where data is stored at rest): A technical region setting and contractual DPA commitment (modeled here as EU server residency).
Data Sovereignty (Which authorities can compel disclosure): Determined by the processor's corporate parent structure, sub-processors, and extraterritorial statutes (requiring Transfer Impact Assessments and supplementary safeguards where applicable).

2.2 Evidentiary Preparedness ([Status: Designed])

Residency Configuration Record: Dated administrative console capture stored in 12_Compliance (I-4).
Executed Art. 28 DPA & Sub-processor List: Indexed for retrieval within 5 minutes.
Processor Security Attestations: Reviewed annually against active scope (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701, and SOC 2 Type II, verifying the exact legal entity covered by each certificate).


3. Proposed Personal Data Inventory & Lawful-Basis Candidates
This register structures Art. 30 Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) and Subject Access Request (SAR) scoping for DPO review:

3.1 T5 Onboarding: Why Employee Consent & Individual Wellbeing Scores Are Avoided (R26, D8)

Imbalance of Power on Employee Consent: Earlier drafts mapped T5 satisfaction/wellbeing fields to Art. 6(1)(a) Consent. Because of the structural imbalance of power between employer and employee, consent in employment is rarely considered freely given (see Article 29 Data Protection Working Party, Opinion 2/2017 on data processing at work (WP 249, adopted 8 June 2017), https://ec.europa.eu/newsroom/article29/item-detail.cfm?item_id=610169, accessed 2026-11-26).
GDPR Art. 9 Special-Category Risk: Recording individual "wellbeing", stress, or health-adjacent notes alongside named employee IDs risks capturing Art. 9 special-category health data without an Art. 9(2) condition.
Proposed Split (D8):
T5 stores strictly objective ramp milestones (training completion, calibration pass/fail, buddy assignment) proposed under Art. 6(1)(f) with a written LIA and 90-day post-ramp anonymization.
Sentiment feedback is separated into an optional, non-identifiable aggregate cohort pulse (minimum aggregation threshold k >= 5 respondents, no user handle or timestamp joinable to T4, and free-text disabled or scrubbed so no Art. 9 data enters governance tables).



3.2 T10 Audit Log: Lawful Basis, Retention Rank & Erasure Balancing (R27, D8)

Art. 6(1)(c) vs. Art. 6(1)(f): GDPR Art. 6(1)(c) applies only where processing is required by a specific Union or Member State legal obligation to which the controller is subject. Unless counsel identifies a binding sector statute mandating bot-command logs, T10 is instead proposed under Art. 6(1)(f) Legitimate Interests (maintaining Art. 32 access security, detecting unauthorized cross-market queries, and verifying administrative integrity), supported by a documented LIA.
Retention Comparison: T10 does not carry the longest retention in the architecture: active T10 partitions are held for 12 months before archive/purge, whereas Internal Area 11 (Client Accounts) retains B2B relationship context across multi-year active client engagements.
Art. 17 Erasure & Art. 21 Objection Handling: T10 is neither automatically exempt from all erasure requests nor uniquely exempt across the organization (statutory holds or Art. 17(3)(e) establishment/exercise/defence of legal claims may also restrict erasure elsewhere). When a data subject submits an Art. 17 erasure or Art. 21 objection request covering T10, the Data Contact/DPO evaluates on a case-by-case basis whether compelling legitimate security/audit grounds (Art. 21(1)) or Art. 17(3)(b)/(e) exceptions require retaining integrity-critical log entries until the 12-month expiry, or whether actor identifiers can be pseudonymized without breaking audit continuity. This policy is disclosed in the workforce privacy notice at onboarding.


4. Personal Data Breach Response Protocol (Art. 33 & Art. 34, R29)

Statutory Rule vs. Internal Escalation Clock: Under EDPB Guidelines 9/2022 on personal data breach notification under GDPR (Version 2.0, adopted 28 March 2023, paras. 31-41, https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2023-04/edpb_guidelines_202209_personal_data_breach_notification_v2.0_en.pdf, accessed 2026-11-26), the 72-hour supervisory notification period under Art. 33(1) runs from when the controller has a reasonable degree of certainty that a security incident compromising personal data has occurred (allowing a brief initial investigation after an alert, while containment and documentation begin immediately). As a conservative internal operational policy, this runbook starts internal SLA tracking at Hour 0 upon first staff or detector alert so internal escalation cannot consume the statutory window.
Risk Threshold & Mandatory Internal Register (Art. 33(1) & Art. 33(5)):
Art. 33(5) Universal Duty: Every personal data breach (facts, effects, and remedial action taken) must be recorded in the internal Breach Register regardless of risk severity.
Art. 33(1) Notification Branch: If assessment indicates the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, supervisory notification is not required, provided the reasoning is documented in the Art. 33(5) register and signed off by the Data Contact/DPO. Otherwise, notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours (using phased notification under Art. 33(4) if forensic details are still developing).
Art. 34(1) Data-Subject Branch: Where the breach is likely to result in a high risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, communicate the breach to affected data subjects without undue delay.






Hour Window (Internal Policy Clock)
Parallel Required Actions
Responsible Role (Defined in Ch. VII)




0 to 2 (Immediate & Parallel)
Contain immediately (revoke compromised tokens/scopes, isolate affected containers, pause Bot writes if needed) in parallel with initial triage to establish whether personal data is involved. Open Art. 33(5) Breach Register entry.
System Administrator (ADM) + Data Contact / DPO


0 to 4
Assess scope, categories/approximate volume of subjects and records, likely consequences, and risk tier (unlikely risk vs. risk vs. high risk).
Data Contact / DPO + ADM


4 to 12
Verify containment held; if unlikely to result in a risk, record reasoned Art. 33(5) determination with legal/DPO sign-off. If high risk, prepare Art. 34 subject communication.
Data Contact / DPO + Upper Management (UPM)


12 to 24
Dispatch Art. 34 communication to affected individuals where high-risk threshold is met (subject to Art. 34(3) exceptions).
Data Contact / DPO


24 to 48
Draft supervisory authority notification package (Art. 33(3) required elements, or initial phased submission under Art. 33(4)).
Data Contact / DPO + ADM


48 to 72 (Ceiling)
Submit supervisory authority notification (without undue delay; never later than 72h from controller awareness) and log filing receipt in Art. 33(5) register.
Data Contact / DPO



4.1 Tracked Security Fault Triggers ([Status: Designed])

F-019 (Container Permission Drift): Unexpected exposure on restricted internal areas (11_Client_Accounts, 12_Compliance, or 13_Confidential).
F-023 (Incomplete Leaver Deprovisioning): Departed user account retains active workspace or container grants past offboarding cutoff.
M14 / Layer-Isolation Fault: B2B contact details inadvertently drafted into a Public_Information_Layer staging node.


5. Internal Layer Specific Safeguards
5.1 Area 11: Client Accounts (I-2 Read / I-3 Write, Market-Scoped)
Holds business-to-business client contact records. Market-scoped container permissions enforce need-to-know access per jurisdiction, and GDPR Art. 9 special-category personal data is strictly prohibited.
5.2 Area 15: Work-Continuity Draft Space (R28)
Earlier designs labeled Area 15 contents "Unknown", creating ambiguity around employee privacy expectations at offboarding. Area 15 is strictly defined as Work-in-Progress Operational Drafts:

Prohibition of Private Content: Area 15 is an employer-governed work-continuity drafting scratchpad (I-0 during active work). Storing private personal files, personal correspondence, medical notes, or any Art. 9 data in Area 15 is expressly prohibited by acceptable-use policy and Banner-disclosed when the folder is provisioned.
HR / Data Contact Review Gate Before Manager Transfer: Upon offboarding (DT-003), Area 15 is not transferred blindly to a line manager. Within the 48-hour offboarding window, HR or the Data Contact/DPO conducts a title/metadata scoping screen to quarantine or delete any inadvertently stored private item; only verified business-continuity drafts transfer to the FLM/MGR.


6. Annual Compliance & Incident Tabletop Drill ([Status: Designed])
Operational readiness is tested annually via a timed simulation with counsel/DPO participation:

[ ] Data Contact / DPO walks through Art. 33(1) (72h rule + risk exception), Art. 33(5) breach register logging, and competent supervisory authority contacts.
[ ] System Administrator (ADM) revokes a test user's access across Platform, Wiki Branch, Database, and Bot layers within 30 minutes (Hour 0 containment).
[ ] Specific T10 incident records are exported and verified within 10 minutes.
[ ] Executed Art. 28 DPA and EU residency configuration evidence are retrieved within 5 minutes.
[ ] End-to-end simulation confirms parallel containment (Hour 0) and  notification readiness.

3. The Mover Protocol (Cross-Market Transfers)
The most frequent lifecycle event, and the most dangerous vector for permission drift. When an agent changes markets but keeps ownership of files in their old market, they can edit content outside their new scope while locking out the incoming owner.

4. Offboarding (The Leaver Protocol)

6. P1 Incident Response SLA ([Status: Designed])
A P1 requires a 2-hour SLA from detection to resolution.

The Three P1 Faults

F-013b (Persistent Audit Log Write Failure): T10 is rejecting writes; state-mutating operations halt until restored. (Note: transient retry latency F-013a operates in buffered Degraded mode while read/scanner telemetry continues.)
F-019 (Restricted Content Breach): Revoke immediately, trigger 72-hour breach assessment clock.

2.1 Why HTML rather than a hosted app
A prototype behind a login is a prototype nobody opens. These can be attached to an email, and the person receiving them does not need an account, a sandbox or a working internet connection.
2.2 Why separate files rather than one
Thirteen flows and ten dashboards in a single component would take several seconds to parse and would be unpleasant to edit. Splitting them costs nothing, because they share no state.

3. The flows
Thirteen sequences. Every one has a failure branch you can trigger, and that is the filter for whether a flow earned its place.

3.3 The two to open with
Flow 01, publish sequence. Step through it once cleanly. Then press Break the move and watch the register correctly hold at Awaiting Approval, which is the system behaving.
Then press both toggles together, Break the move and Write state first, and step through. The register announces Published while the document never left staging.
Both toggles, not one. With buggy ordering alone the move still succeeds, so the register is only briefly wrong and corrects itself. The permanent lie needs the write to happen early and the move to fail, which is exactly the combination that occurs in production.
The panel that appears reads the register is lying. That is the single most consequential failure mode in the platform, and it produces no error message.
Flow 12, verification. Switch to Draft first and step through. The author writes ten working days from memory, the search returns fifteen to twenty, and the author keeps ten because they have already written it.
The published file is wrong, reads exactly like a correct file, and scores 100 on health. More review does not catch this, which is why the protocol puts identification before drafting rather than checking afterwards.

05, provisioning preview. Press Preview it. A scope change writes hundreds of grants and there is otherwise no way to see what it will do before it does it. The preview also surfaces the nine files that would be left outside the new scope.
06, verification findings. The number is falling and the caption says watch it, do not celebrate it. A falling findings count can mean quality improving or checking stopping, and the dashboard cannot tell you which.

Means

XII. Architecture Decision Records & Governance
Focus: 12 Core ADRs, Governance RACI & Platform Change Watch

1. The 12 Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
Every structural constraint in this architecture exists to prevent a specific silent failure. Each record documents the rejected alternative and the exact failure mode triggered if a future team attempts to simplify it.



ID
Decision
Rejected Alternative
Architectural Rationale
What Breaks If This Changes




ADR-01
Single Private Space, Two Root Nodes
Separate spaces for Public and Internal estates
Unifies 3,055 public reference nodes (3,000+) and ~1,200 initial internal nodes under one deny-by-default administration surface.
Doubles admin overhead and breaks cross-linking between internal SOPs and the public files they govern.


ADR-02
Data Layer (9 Tables) vs. Audit Layer (2 Tables) Split
Single database housing all 11 tables
Isolates bounded operational state (~6,300 rows by Year 3) from high-volume audit logs (T10, T-KPI-02).
Audit log growth degrades operational queries and prevents read-only managers from saving custom dashboards.


ADR-03
Container-Level Permission Inheritance
Per-document ACL management
Permissions attach to folder containers (perm_type: "container") across 5 internal tiers (I-0..I-4) and inherit on publish move.
Per-document ACLs create untraceable drift across 40 markets and break nightly permission reconciliation (SC-004).


ADR-04
Move-Then-Confirm Async Publish
Write Published state first, then move node
Bot polls async move task and asserts parent_node_token before writing Published to T1.
Writing state first produces the "register is lying" failure mode whenever an async move fails silently.


ADR-05
Agent Lockdown via Bot Proxy
Granting frontline agents direct edit rights on T1
Agents (60 frontline AGT seats in the 100-seat reference model) are strictly View-Only on base tables; state updates execute exclusively via Bot commands.
Direct cell editing across dozens of seats corrupts register integrity and bypasses T10 audit logging.


ADR-06
Native Date Mirror (Review Due)
Triggering automations off formula fields
Bot copies formula-computed review dates into a native date field on every write.
Platform automations cannot reliably trigger off formula fields; the daily scan silently misses overdue files.


ADR-07
Stepped Health Score Deduction (Needs Review )
Linear 1-point-per-day overdue deduction
Non-linear jump at Day 15 to 30 (-28 pts -> score 72, below Healthy >= 80) forces status into Needs Review immediately after an ignored Day-14 escalation.
Linear scoring leaves Days 15 to 20 at 85 to 80 (Healthy), masking ignored Day-14 FLM escalations.


ADR-08
Single Daily Review Scan (07:30 UTC)
Per-record date trigger automations
Replaces ~1,700 monthly per-record platform automation runs with 30 monthly daily-trigger runs (98.2% reduction).
Per-record triggers burn platform automation quotas and scatter escalation logic across untestable UI rules.


ADR-09
Native JS SDK Console
Standalone web app using a Bot service token
Console loads client-side under the signed-in user's identity inside the workspace.
A standalone web app attributes every human admin action to "The Bot," destroying audit attribution.


ADR-10
Declarative KPIs + Version Breaks
Hardcoded dashboard metrics
KPIs live as JSON rows in T-KPI-03; filter edits auto-increment Definition Version.
Editing a KPI filter silently corrupts historical trend lines by comparing mismatched definitions.


ADR-11
Revoke-Before-Grant Mover Protocol
Granting new market access before revoking old
Departing market tokens are stripped before new market grants are provisioned.
Granting first creates a compliance window where a mover holds dual-market access simultaneously.


ADR-12
Two-Administrator Continuity Rule
Single named platform owner
Minimum two named administrators against every credential, secret, and archive surface.
Bus-Factor-1 creates an unrecoverable lockout risk during offboarding or P1 incidents.

3. Platform Change Watch Protocol
Waiting for bi-annual review dates fails when an external platform or regulator changes rules mid-quarter. The Platform Change Watch intercepts breaking changes out-of-cycle:

Signal Intake: Regulatory updates, API deprecations, or policy shifts are logged as a Change Watch event with an effective date and affected domain codes (POL, VRT, FMT, ONB).
Blast-Radius Query: Console queries T1 by folder code and market (CC) to produce the exact list of impacted nodes.
Forced Review Override: Bot sets Status = Needs Review and resets Review Due (native) to T + 5 working days across impacted rows, bypassing standard cadence.
Verification Closure: Impacted files cannot return to Active until Last Source Verification is updated against the new primary source and logged in T10.


4. Benefits Realisation & Telemetry Cadence
Value tracking combines automated operational telemetry with external validation:

ADR-010: Single-Repository Static & Interactive Separation (X8)

Decision: Maintain one public repository where the static HonKit documentation build (_book/) ships cleanly to GitHub Pages with zero backend dependencies or live AI code (D10).
Guardrail: The public static build serves deterministic Replay surfaces and offline editors only, never exposing live proxy URLs or server credentials.

ADR-011: Standardized Lean Reference Model (X2)

Decision: Replace all employer-derived metrics and proprietary workspace names in public documentation with a transparent, parameterized 100-seat Lean DMADV reference model across 40 markets and 3,055 public reference nodes (3,000+ nodes).
Rationale: Eliminates confidentiality risk while allowing engineering leaders and reviewers to verify every calculation directly.

ADR-012: Self-Hosted ALTCHA Proof-of-Work for Bot Protection (X4)

Decision: Use self-hosted ALTCHA proof-of-work on grant request endpoints instead of third-party CAPTCHA scripts.
Rationale: Preserves zero third-party script requests and zero third-party visitor IP telemetry while running entirely inside stateless server routes.

ADR-013: Free-Only Config-Driven Model Registry (X7)

Decision: Admit only card-free LLM endpoints that pass a 7-point primary-source admission gate (no payment card, public portfolio demo permitted, documented data/training terms, region noted, RPM/RPD/TPM/context quotas documented, HTTP 429 at limit rather than billing, and JSON mode support recorded) behind a versioned routing config.

ADR-014: Browser-Native Charts and BI Export Over Server-Side Plotting

Decision: Render interactive SSoT and Syndicate dashboards using self-hosted browser-side JavaScript charts paired with one-click normalized CSV and JSON exports for Tableau and Power BI.
Rationale: Keeps serverless bundles compact and offline-capable while delivering clean datasets directly consumable by enterprise BI tools.

2. Acceptance Criteria Matrix (Representative Assertions)

3. API Contract & Fault-Tolerance Boundaries
3.1 Batch & Rate-Limit Contract

Chunk Ceiling: Maximum 500 records per batch read/write call.
Atomicity Guard: Because vendor batch writes are all-or-nothing, client-side schema validation runs locally on all 500 rows before transmission.
HTTP 429 Backoff Policy:




Retry Attempt
Wait Strategy
Action on Failure




Attempts 1 to 4
Respect Retry-After header; fallback exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s, 16s) + jitter
Re-attempt identical idempotent payload


Attempt 5 (Final)
32s backoff
Abort batch, preserve local cursor, log F-011 (429_EXHAUSTED) to T10, alert Admin



3.2 Webhook Callback Contract (The 3-Second Rule)
Every interactive card callback must return HTTP 200 within 3,000 ms containing a non-blocking status toast. Downstream wiki moves, polling loops, and database writes execute asynchronously via worker queue. Exceeding 3 seconds triggers platform retry storms and duplicate state mutations.

4. Deterministic Test Fixtures (Zero Clock Reads)
A test fixture that calls Date.now() passes on build day and breaks 15 days later when mock records cross escalation thresholds.

Fixed Anchor: Every date in the test dataset is computed as REFERENCE_DATE + offset_days.
Coherent Shift: Advancing REFERENCE_DATE shifts the entire corpus in lockstep while preserving exact boundary states:




Fixture Record
Offset Formula
Resulting State Under Test




FIX-001 (Healthy)
Next Review = REF + 45d
Active, Health Score 100


FIX-002 (Escalation Edge)
Next Review = REF - 14d
Triggers Day-14 FLM escalation card


FIX-003 (Stepped Penalty)
Next Review = REF - 20d
Days Overdue = 20, Health Score 72 (verifies stepped -28 penalty vs. -20 linear)


FIX-004 (Kill-Switch Edge)
Next Review = REF - 30d
Surfaces in Console S7 Archive Queue (final intervention window before midnight archive)




5. String Catalogue & Reviewer Calibration
5.1 String Catalogue Governance
All user-facing copy is centralized by ID (STR-WARN-STALE, STR-ERR-SCOPE, STR-ESC-DAY14, STR-CONF-PUBLISH) rather than scattered across handlers. Updating a compliance disclaimer requires a single catalogue edit and guarantees uniform rendering across DM cards, channel replies, and Console toasts.
5.2 Reviewer Calibration (Measurement System Analysis)
Human reviewers are treated as a measurement instrument and calibrated prior to live market waves:

Blinded Corpus: Six realistic test files (CALIB_A to CALIB_F) seeded with deliberate failure modes (subtle threshold errors, swap-test failures, missing source classifications, ceiling-vs-floor budget errors).
Key Isolation: The answer key (CALIB_00_FACILITATOR) is strictly withheld from reviewers before scoring.
Release Gate: Reviewers must reach >80% inter-rater agreement against the calibration key before receiving publish-approval permissions.

14-AI-Content-Engineering-and-Rules.html.body:
XIV. AI Content Engineering & Verification Rules
Focus: Two Writing Standards, 15 Mechanical Checks & 5 Semantic Gates

1. The Two Writing Depth Standards
Scaling 3,055 public reference files (3,000+ nodes) across 40 markets requires rigid structural blueprints so every file answers its operational question without fluff. Every domain maps to one of two formal standards:
1.1 The Activation-Depth Standard (VRT, POL, MKT, LIF, CAM, ONB)
A market or vertical playbook is incomplete unless it contains all seven mandatory components:



#
Mandatory Component
Operational Requirement




1
Named Entities
Exact local regulators, statutory decrees, and payment rails, never generic placeholders ("the relevant authority").


2
Hard Numbers
Specific verifiable thresholds and statutory limits wherever knowable; ranges are a fallback, never a default.


3
Decision Tables
Every branching choice or eligibility matrix is rendered as a structured comparison table, never buried in prose.


4
Phased Rollout + Exit Gates
Execution broken into sequential phases with explicit quantitative go/no-go exit criteria between phases.


5
Local-Language Register
Market-specific language and idioms matching the exact jurisdiction (omitted for ONB technical setup files).


6
Verification Checklist
A closing pre-launch checklist the operator can physically tick through before going live.


7
Classified Sources
Every external claim backed by a primary source explicitly classified as Verified or Needs Confirmation.



1.2 The Integration-Guide Standard (FMT, structural TPL)
Global technical guides follow a strict 5-part sequence per tool or integration:

Intro Paragraph: Scope and exact target use case.
Prerequisites: Required account tiers, admin permissions, and SDK/plugin versions.

The Swap-the-Country-Name Test: Replace the country name with a neighboring market. If the guidance still reads plausibly, the file lacks local specificity and is rejected.
Named Entity Verification: Confirm statutory bodies, tax/VAT rules, and local payment rails are current and legally exact.
Regional Linguistic Register: Enforce strict regional boundaries (e.g., Flemish vs. Netherlands Dutch; formal vs. informal address).

4. The Anti-Anchoring Research Protocol
Writing a draft first and fact-checking afterward fails because human reviewers anchor to fluent AI prose (RPN 560). The generation workflow reverses the sequence:

Extract Perishable Claims First: List every UI path, legal threshold, fee, and partner availability flag before drafting.
Dual-Source Load-Bearing Facts: Verify every high-impact claim against primary documentation.
Surface Conflicts Explicitly: When two official sources disagree, document the conflict rather than silently picking one.
Draft Last: Assemble the file only after the verified fact table is locked.

XVI. Signal Press: Client-Side Document Designer
Signal Studio (Chapter XI) solves 16:9 presentation design by separating structured JSON content from theme rendering. Signal Press extends the exact same principle to portrait A4 operational documents (210mm x 297mm), targeting Microsoft Word (.docx), Google Docs, enterprise wikis, selectable-text Dark and Light PDFs, inline-CSS Email HTML, and Markdown.

Launch Offline Editor: Open Signal Press (Browser-Only Offline Mode)
Companion Slide Surface: Open Signal Studio (16:9 Slide Editor)


1. Architectural Premise: Theme-Free Content, Surface-Specific Rendering
Most document generators fail across enterprise tools because they hardcode visual styling into the authored text or export dark-canvas graphics into word processors where reviewers cannot edit them cleanly.
Signal Press enforces three strict invariants:

Manual-First, Zero-Network Offline Core: Editing, template switching, Markdown/JSON import, pre-export linting, and .docx / PDF / HTML / Markdown generation run completely inside the browser. Nothing leaves the tab in offline mode, and localStorage autosave is off by default with a one-click clear control.
Theme-Free Block Schema (signal-press-doc-v1): Content is authored as typed blocks (heading, paragraph, bullets, numbered, table, kpi_row, callout, quote, hero_image, divider, source_note, page_break, toc) plus explicit source provenance (verified, reported, unconfirmable). Colour roles and typography are bound only at render time.
Surface-Appropriate Export Parity:
DOCX, Google Docs, and Enterprise Wikis: Always render on the Signal Light surface (#FFFFFF ground, #14161C ink, #F5F6F8 table banding, #B80D42 deep pink, #0A7571 deep cyan tuned to 5.53:1 for 8.5pt A4 eyebrows) using metric-matched Calibri / Carlito styles. Callouts export as single-cell shaded OOXML tables rather than floating Word textboxes so Google Docs and enterprise wikis preserve flow without converting callouts into uneditable drawing canvases.
A4 PDF (Dark and Print-Safe Light): Renders semantic HTML with @page { size: A4 portrait; margin: 14mm 15mm }, self-hosted Carlito (SIL OFL-1.1), selectable text, and WCAG AA contrast (>= 4.5:1) in both Console Dark (#0B0C10) and Light Screen (#FFFFFF).
Email-Body HTML: Client-facing follow-ups export as 600px table-based HTML with 100% inline CSS and zero external image or font requests, surviving Gmail, Outlook Word-engine tables, and Apple Mail without PDF attachments.

Enterprise and commercial teams adopting generative AI routinely hit three structural failure modes:

Vendor & Model Lock-In: Hardcoding a single provider SDK or transient free-tier model slug breaks production workflows whenever rate limits tighten or model deprecations occur.
Unbounded Jurisdiction & PII Drift: Routing EU prospect context, draft contracts, or internal playbooks through consumer chat interfaces or non-EU free pools exposes unmasked identifiers (VAT, IBAN, personal emails) outside approved processing boundaries.
Hallucinated Entity Facts: Asking an LLM to "research a company" from parametric memory fabricates registration numbers, e-commerce stacks, and pixel configurations that erode credibility in technical discovery calls.

Balaerion resolves all three failure modes through a dual-mode serverless AI gateway operating from one unified codebase and pre-dispatch security boundary:

Balaerion II. Hosting & Failover Topology
Focus: Serverless Edge Execution, Hybrid pgvector + tsvector Retrieval, Replay-First Resilience & Lane-Isolated Provider Failover · Status: Prototype + Designed

1. Serverless Execution Topology
Balaerion eliminates idle container cost and persistent server patching by combining stateless serverless compute with an isolated EU PostgreSQL persistence and vector layer:

Stateless Compute & UI (Next.js App Router): Renders passive documentation, Replay consoles, and offline Signal Press tools with zero session cookies, while funneling all live LLM, SSoT retrieval, and OSINT operations through typed server route handlers.
Persistence & Hybrid Search (PostgreSQL EU + pgvector): Reached exclusively from server routes using a server-only service_role key. Row-Level Security (RLS) is enabled on every table (grants, cooldown_hashes, altcha_replay_nonces, rate_limit_counters, daily_usage_circuit, ssot_documents, ssot_chunks) with zero anon or authenticated public policies.
Quota-Aware Provider Failover: Within lane: general, the router orders candidate providers starting with the user's selected provider followed by healthy configured peers. Upstream HTTP 429, 5xx, or timeout (12,000 ms abort signal) advances immediately to the next admitted provider in the same lane. Cross-lane failover from eu to general is structurally impossible.

[Reviewer / Architect Browser]
   |-- Passive / Replay (0 Cookies) -----------> [Next.js App Router UI (Local Replay)]
   |-- Grant Cookie or Owner Session ----------> [Server Proxy: /api/chat & /api/osint]
                                                        |
                                        1. enforcePreDispatchGate() (PII + Lane Lock)
                                        2. SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (Supabase EU Postgres RLS)
                                        3. search_ssot_hybrid() (tsvector GIN + pgvector HNSW)
                                                        |
                        +-------------------------------+-------------------------------+
                        | (lane: eu ONLY)                                               | (lane: general)
                        v                                                               v
        [EU Safe Pool: Mistral · Codestral · OVH]                     [General Pool: NVIDIA · Groq · Cerebras · Gemini]
                        | (if all throttled -> 0 cross-lane!)                           | (if all throttled)
                        +-------------------------------> [Deterministic Replay Floor] 

2. Request Path & Graceful Degradation
Every /api/chat and /api/press/assist invocation traverses a deterministic 6-step execution pipeline:

Replay Mode Short-Circuit (Default): Unauthenticated visitors (or requests when Supabase / provider keys are unset) receive deterministic Replay responses immediately with HTTP 200 / 401 replay: true and zero database writes.
Session & Owner Verification: isOwnerAuthenticated(request) checks the HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict owner session first (granting unlimited live calls for the portfolio owner). Otherwise authorizeAndReserveGrantTokens() validates the HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax single-use reviewer cookie.
Pre-Dispatch Controls (enforcePreDispatchGate): Before any token reservation or network socket opens, deterministic regexes scan the prompt and conversation history for VAT numbers, IBANs, emails, and phone patterns, and verify that the requested provider matches the target lane (eu default when unclassified). Violations return HTTP 403 with 0 tokens deducted.
Atomic Weighted-Token Reservation & Global Circuit Breaker: PostgreSQL locks the grant row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), checks daily_usage_circuit against the global daily ceiling, and reserves ceil(estimated_tokens * provider_weight).
Hybrid SSoT Grounding (search_ssot_hybrid): When invoked from /ssot or Mode B ProspectHub, the server embeds the query via card-free 1024-dim multilingual embeddings (Cloudflare @cf/baai/bge-m3 -> Cohere embed-multilingual-v3.0 -> null lexical fallback) and executes Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) combining PostgreSQL tsvector (GIN) and pgvector (HNSW cosine similarity), scoped strictly to market IN (active_market, 'GLOBAL').
Bounded Failover & Replay Floor: The router attempts configured providers within the resolved lane under per-provider abort timeouts. If every configured provider in that lane is throttled or unreachable, the gateway returns a labeled deterministic Replay response rather than crashing or crossing lanes.


3. Zero-Commit Google Drive SSoT Ingestion Pipeline
To keep internal or commercial playbooks out of public Git history while making them queryable in /ssot and ProspectHub, Balaerion implements a Zero-Commit In-Memory Ingestion Pipeline:

Focus: Pre-Dispatch Lane Enforcement, Invite-Only Reviewer Grant Cryptography, Zero-Cookie ePrivacy Posture & GDPR Controls · Status: Prototype + Designed

1. Two-Lane Routing (lane: eu vs. lane: general)
Balaerion enforces a deterministic cryptographic and regex boundary between EU-scoped synthesis and general prompting before any request leaves the server proxy or reserves grant budget:

1.1 Deterministic Pre-Dispatch Gate (enforcePreDispatchGate)
Rather than trusting an LLM to redact sensitive strings after ingestion, lane-guard.ts executes synchronous deterministic checks across both the current prompt and conversation history:

Identifier Pattern Rejection: Blocks EU VAT numbers (BE0..., NL...B01, FR...), IBANs, email addresses, and phone numbers before upstream dispatch (HTTP 403, 0 tokens charged).
Provider-to-Lane Binding: Rejects any payload attempting to pair lane: eu with a general provider ID (groq, nvidia-nim, gemini, etc.), preventing modified client requests from bypassing UI dropdowns.
Output Schema & Markdown Sanitization: Responses rendered into Signal Studio or Signal Press pass through deterministic JSON/block validators (H6 single-pass repair ceiling) with zero raw HTML dangerouslySetInnerHTML execution.


2. Database Isolation, Leak Gate & Hard Refusals

Server-Only Database Access: PostgreSQL runs in an EU region (eu-central-1 or eu-west-1) with ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on every table and zero public CREATE POLICY grants. Browser clients hold zero database credentials for sensitive tables.
Automated Pre- & Post-Build Leak Gate (scripts/leak_gate.py): Scans all tracked Markdown, TypeScript, JSON, SVG, and compiled _book/ HTML artifacts for internal employer nomenclature, secret prefixes (nvapi-, gsk_, sk-or-), unlisted deployment origins, and typographical regressions.
Architectural Hard Refusals:
Never reuse personal consumer chat subscriptions (ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro session cookies) via reverse proxies.
Never log raw prompts, raw IP addresses, raw grant codes, or visitor emails in PostgreSQL tables.
Never auto-mint live LLM access to unverified public traffic.




3. GDPR & Deterministic Fact Boundary ([Status: Prototype + Designed])

Deterministic Fact Boundary: Legal entity names, registration numbers (KBO, KvK, SIREN), DNS/ESP records, CMS platforms, and advertising pixels originate exclusively from structured OSINT collectors (src/lib/osint/engine.ts) or synthetic calibration fixtures. Where a signal cannot be verified deterministically, personas must output unconfirmable rather than guessing.
PII Scrubbing on OSINT Snippets: Before any external search snippet (Tavily, Serper, FR SIREN) enters server RAM or a prompt context, scrubPersonalIdentifiers() strips personal email and telephone patterns so corporate tech-stack enrichment never ingests personal contact data.
Data Minimization & Retention (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) & Art. 5(1)(e)):
Zero Passive Cookies (ePrivacy Directive Art. 5(3) Criterion B): Passive browsing, Replay Mode, and Offline Signal Press set zero cookies and load zero analytics scripts. The balaerion_grant cookie (HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax) is set strictly after an explicit user click redeeming a grant code on /redeem.
Automated Hourly Purge (pg_cron): Expired rate-limit counters (1h window, keyed by daily-rotating salted IP hash HMAC-SHA256(pepper || UTC_DATE, ip)), single-use ALTCHA nonces (5m TTL), and expired grants (+7d post-expiry) are purged hourly, alongside a daily cleanup of cron.job_run_details.


Human-in-the-Loop Governance: AI personas propose briefs, diagnostic questions, and slide/document drafts; every lifecycle transition and external outreach action requires explicit human review and execution.


4. Abuse Prevention, Invite-Only Approval Queue & Budget Ceilings
Because a public portfolio linked on GitHub and resumes can attract automated scrapers or curious visitors, protecting free-tier LLM and transactional email quotas requires layered defense-in-depth:
Reviewer            Public GitHub Pages          Private Workspace (/redeem)       Owner Telegram / (/admin)
   |--- Browse Docs & Demos (0 Login, 0 Cookies) --->|                                       |
   |--- Request 48h Reviewer Grant (Issue / Form) ------------------------------>|           |

4.1 Five Quota-Protection Layers ([Status: Implemented & Verified])

Invite-Only Default + Manual Owner Approval (GRANT_APPROVAL_MODE=owner_approval): Submitting the request form on /redeem never auto-mints a BLR-... grant. After passing self-hosted SHA-256 ALTCHA proof-of-work, nonce replay burn, and a 3 requests / hour daily-rotating salted IP limit, the server sends a private approval alert to TELEGRAM_OWNER_ID. Only the owner can mint grants on /admin.
Salted HMAC Grant Storage: Raw BLR-XXXXXXXXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX codes are displayed once at mint time and never stored in PostgreSQL; only a public kid, 16-byte random salt, and HMAC-SHA256(pepper, salt || normalized_code) are persisted.
URL Fragment Delivery & Scanner-Safe Explicit Click: Share links place the secret inside #code=BLR-... (which browsers never transmit in HTTP GET request lines or server logs). Client JS scrubs window.location.hash via history.replaceState on load and waits for an explicit button click so enterprise email/Slack link-preview bots cannot burn single-use codes.
Per-Grant Atomic Ceilings: Default reviewer grants cap exposure at 25 live calls, 12,000 weighted tokens, and a 48-hour issue TTL (24 hours post-redemption), enforced atomically via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.
Global Daily Circuit Breaker: Even if multiple approved reviewers test simultaneously, daily_usage_circuit enforces a hard daily workspace ceiling across all grants, failing closed to Replay Mode until 00:00 UTC.

Parametric Fabrication: Without live DNS, HTML , and business registry inspection, the model guesses whether the merchant runs Shopify or Lightspeed, guesses whether Consent Mode v2 is active, and invents plausible-sounding registration numbers.

1. The Problem & Target Outcome
Recreational football prediction groups and informal analytics spreadsheets fail consistently across three dimensions:

Cognitive & Recency Bias in Probability Estimation: Human tipsters overweight last weekend's headline scoreline (3-0 from 0.8 xG), ignore low-score draw correlation (0-0 and 1-1), and compare raw probabilities against bookmaker prices without stripping asymmetric overround (vig).
Hindsight & Post-Kickoff Mutation: Selection threads in group chats blur tentative opinions with locked commitments, creating post-lineup or in-play disputes over which picks actually counted.
Spreadsheet Entry/Exit Dilution: Equal-split spreadsheets punish early participants whenever a new member joins after a profitable matchday run, or break completely when a member partially redeems virtual units mid-season.
